newsitem.title: USA: Suspect in Saudi bombing in Iran - report.
newsitem.headline: Suspect in Saudi bombing in Iran - report.

text.p: The alleged mastermind of the bombing that killed 19 U.S. airmen in Saudi Arabia last year is believed to be living in Iran under protection of its government, Newsday reported on Saturday.

The newspaper said the fact the Saudi bomb-plot suspect had been given safe haven by the Iranians gave credence to growing evidence that Iran played a major role in the attack. The tabloid also said American and Canadian intelligence officials believed Syria gave tacit approval to the June 25 bombing near Dhahran.

A top Saudi Shiite operative fled to Syria after the attack and crossed into Iran, a U.S. counterterrorism specialist familiar with the bombing investigation told Newsday. A court document filed in Canada on Thursday identified the alleged mastermind as Ahmed Ibrahim Ahmad Mughassil.

The newspaper's source said Mughassil "lives under the protection of, as a guest of, the Iranian government." A second U.S. source confirmed to the tabloid that Mughassil had been living in Iran, but added, without elaborating, that he and other suspects in the bombing "may be moving around."
U.S. officials declined to comment on the information or say what kind of response the Clinton administration was considering, the newspaper said.

The Canadian document came to light during a deportation hearing against another suspect in the bombing, Hani Abdel-Rahim Hussein al-Sayegh, who is being held in Canada. The newspaper said U.S. sources believed Sayegh drove the car that signalled the bomb-laden truck to enter the Khobar Towers parking lot.
Sayegh was arrested in Ottawa on March 18 on the grounds that he represented a security threat to Canada.

The sources also told Newsday the Saudi dissidents had been given religious training in the holy city of Qom inside Iran. The report said some of the Saudi Shiites recruited by an Iranian intelligence operative also received military training from the Iranian-supported Hezbollah organisation.
